domain_restrictions: f is a function with domain A and codomain B (f: A -> B)
injectivity: for all a1, a2 in A, if a1 != a2 then f(a1) != f(a2) (equivalently f(a1)=f(a2) implies a1=a2)
cardinality |A| and |B| are interpreted as natural numbers (implicitly requires finiteness)
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all sets A and B, if A and B are finite and there exists an injective function f: A -> B, then the cardinalities satisfy |A| ≤ |B|.

payload.statement_nl: Let A and B be finite sets. If there exists an injective function f from A to B, then the cardinality of A is less than or equal to the cardinality of B.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Let A and B be finite sets, and suppose there exists an injective function f : A -> B. We must prove that |A| <= |B|.

Consider the image of A under f:

S := f(A) = {f(a) : a in A}.

Then S is a subset of B. Since B is finite, every subset of B is finite, so S is finite.

Now regard f as a function from A to S. This map is surjective by the definition of S: every element of S has the form f(a) for some a in A. It is also injective, because f was assumed injective as a map into B, and the injectivity condition does not depend on whether we view the codomain as B or as the smaller set S.

Therefore f : A -> S is a bijection. Hence A and S have the same cardinality:

|A| = |S|.

Since S is a subset of the finite set B, we have

|S| <= |B|.

Combining these two facts gives

|A| = |S| <= |B|,

so |A| <= |B|, as required.

Thus, whenever there exists an injective function from a finite set A to a finite set B, the cardinality of A is less than or equal to the cardinality of B.
result_payload.proof_summary: Take the image S=f(A). The map f: A -> S is bijective because it is injective and onto its image, so |A|=|S|. Since S is a subset of the finite set B, |S|<=|B|. Hence |A|<=|B|.

used_external_facts: If f:A->B and S=f(A), then f:A->S is surjective; if f is injective, then f:A->S is bijective.
Bijection implies equality of cardinalities for finite sets.
If S is a subset of a finite set B, then |S| <= |B|.
